ruleset.name: Explicitness Rules
ruleset.description:
Opt-in checks for implicit inputs and implicit outputs (see "Grokking Simplicity", chapter 3). The explicit inputs of a function are its arguments. The explicit output of a function is its return value. All other data that goes into or comes out of a function is implicit, and makes the function an action.
These rules are not part of the default `go` ruleset. The methods of a type can use their receiver freely. Use `explicitness-strict` to also flag receiver reads and writes.
Run with: messgo <paths> <format> explicitness

rule.name: ImplicitInput
rule.message: The {0} {1}() has an implicit input: {2}. Pass it in as an argument.

property.name: include-receiver
property.description: Also report reads of the receiver of a method.

rule.name: ImplicitOutput
rule.message: The {0} {1}() has an implicit output: {2}. Return it instead.

property.name: include-receiver
property.description: Also report writes through the receiver of a method.
